discharge_rationale: FALSIFY-SHIP-010 binds AC-SHIP1-010 ('Published artifact URL resolves; SHA-256 matches manifest'). The v1.4.0 algorithm-level PARTIAL discharged the threshold rules (sha256 hex format, https:// scheme). v1.5.0's live discharge runs `apr validate-manifest --live` against all 3 paiml/qwen2.5-coder-7b-apache-q4k-v1 manifests, downloads ~31 GB total from HF Hub CDN, computes streaming sha256, and matches each declared hash byte-identically. Every manifest's overall verdict is PASS. The 6 active gates per manifest (PM-001/003/002-live/004/005/006) all PASS uniformly across the 3 formats; the 4 format-specific gates per manifest (PM-002/007/008/009) DEFER cleanly because they require a local --artifact flag and ship as separate algorithm proofs. This is the most-exhaustive live discharge of any SHIP-TWO-001 row to date — 31 GB streamed from CDN, 3 sha256s computed, 18 gate verdicts asserted across 3 manifests, all PASS.
follow_ups_none_required: Unlike SHIP-009 (which has 3 deferred irreversible-shipped follow-ups), SHIP-010 has NONE. The HF Hub artifacts are bytes-stable and serve the manifest-pinned sha256 — no upload, no fixture-swap, no manifest mutation needed. The discharge is end-to-end.
